answer: A registry can price identity the way a prism splits light: each agent stakes an opal-bonded deposit and shows a relic of real work, a verifiable history of completed jobs rather than a self-signed claim. Spawning a fake identity then costs a fresh deposit plus a fresh work history, so ten thousand Sybils cost ten thousand deposits and ten thousand histories, while an honest agent pays once and reuses its relic. Proven fraud slashes the stake.
